brigade:hrhb_101st_oraje_brigade.source: Balkan Battlegrounds: A Military History of the Yugoslav Conflict, 1990-1995, Volume I
brigade:hrhb_101st_oraje_brigade.citation: Volume I, PDF p. 437 / printed 400, verified verbatim in the local corpus at data/derived/knowledge_base/balkan_battlegrounds/pages/BB1_p0437.json: "The Orasje Corps District was originally organized into six brigades: the 101st Bosanski Brod, 102nd Odzak, 103rd Derventa, 104th Samac, 105th Modrica, and 106th Orasje." The page attests ORAŠJE as one of the six original home regions. PDF pp. 437-438 continue: after heavy losses in 1992 and early 1993 the corps was reorganized in the early 1994 HVO restructuring, five of the six brigades having lost their home regions, folded into the 201st and 202nd Home Defence Regiments at Orašje with their old numeric designators retained as battalions. That is WHY the October 1995 order of battle at PDF pp. 481-495 shows the post-consolidation picture: it is an end-of-war snapshot and is not evidence of April 1992 structure.
brigade:hrhb_101st_oraje_brigade.conflict_note: THE PREVIOUS CITATION USED THE OCTOBER 1995 ORDER OF BATTLE (PDF pp. 481-495) TO SOURCE AN APRIL 1992 START — the same wrong-year defect already corrected two rows away on brigade:hrhb_102nd_brigade, whose Orašje home came from that same appendix and belonged at Odžak. An end-of-war appendix describes the post-consolidation structure; it cannot establish opening structure. Re-cited to the p.437 narrative. WHAT IS ATTESTED AND WHAT IS NOT: the home region (Orašje, one of the six) is attested; the ordinal (101st) is not — p.437 assigns 101st to BOSANSKI BROD and gives ORAŠJE the 106th. NOT RESOLVED HERE, DELIBERATELY: same reason as brigade:hrhb_104th_bosanski_brod_brigade — the ordinal correction is a Posavina-wide renumber, territory-affecting, and sequenced separately. Note also that brigade:hrhb_106th_bosanska_posavina_brigade is already homed at Orašje, so the two rows currently share a home region while the source gives the 106th sole claim to it; that overlap is part of the same sequenced correction and is not touched here.

The citation above has been narrowed to the attested half. NOT RESOLVED HERE, DELIBERATELY: correcting the ordinal means renumbering across the Posavina family (per the source, Orašje moves 101st→106th, Bosanski Brod 104th→101st, Šamac gains the 104th), which moves brigades and is territory-affecting. It is sequenced as a separate change. This record must not be read as endorsing the current ordinal, only as no longer misattributing it to p.437.

brigade:rs_5th_podrinje.source: Balkan Battlegrounds: A Military History of the Yugoslav Conflict, 1990-1995, Volume II
brigade:rs_5th_podrinje.citation: MUNICIPALITY ONLY — THIS CITATION DOES NOT COVER THE home_osid. Volume II, PDF p. 310 / printed 291, footnote 121: "Originally 1st GORAZDE Light Infantry Brigade; merged with 2nd Podrinje mid-late 1994, but retained 5th designator." Volume II, PDF p. 416 / printed 397, footnote 42, names the trio "1st Podrinje (Rogatica), 2nd Podrinje (Visegrad), and 5th Podrinje (GORAZDE) Light Infantry Brigades". Balkan Battlegrounds gives the municipality and no settlement for this unit at April 1992. Every settlement-level HQ statement for it — Volume I, PDF p. 502 / printed 465 Appendix G ("HQ Visegrad", July 1995) and Volume I, PDF p. 446 / printed 409 ("from Visegrad") — is POST-MERGER and describes the consolidated unit, not the April 1992 one. Volume II, PDF p. 303 / printed 284 confirms that reading with its "(to mid-late 1994)" markers.
brigade:rs_5th_podrinje.conflict_note: HOME CORRECTED FROM VLASENICA TO GORAŽDE. Balkan Battlegrounds never places this brigade at Vlasenica at any date. THE ERROR HAD A TRACEABLE MECHANISM, recorded because it will recur elsewhere in Appendix G: the appendix reads "Drina Corps, HQ Vlasenica" and then lists the corps troops — 5th Military Police Battalion HQ Vlasenica, 5th Communications HQ Vlasenica, 5th Mixed Artillery HQ Vlasenica, 5th Engineer HQ Vlasenica, 5th Medical HQ Vlasenica — and only THEN the brigades. An eye travelling up the "5th ..., HQ Vlasenica" column from the brigade line lands exactly on Vlasenica. Two tells confirmed transcription rather than sourcing: home_settlement was an empty string, and the sibling brigade:rs_1st_podrinje was correctly homed Rogatica per footnote 117. THE CITATION WAS ALSO CIRCULAR AS A MERGE JUSTIFICATION, which is what deleted the sister brigade: Appendix G is a July 1995 snapshot showing ONE Podrinje brigade at Višegrad precisely BECAUSE it postdates the mid/late-1994 consolidation. That snapshot was then read as proof the merge had always been the case, and brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade was deleted as a duplicate. Both are restored. THREE TRAPS CHECKED AND REJECTED, recorded so they are not re-walked. (1) THE 336th LEAD IS A DEAD END: footnote 121 adds that the brigade was "apparently formed from major elements of the pre-war 336th (ex 4th Armored) Motorized Brigade", but Volume I, PDF p. 201 / printed 164 places 336th elements deploying to the ZVORNIK area in February-March 1992, roughly 100 km from Goražde — chaining the source's own hedge would home this brigade at Zvornik, confidently and wrongly. (2) KOPAČI AND USTIPRAČA ARE THE INTUITIVE ANSWERS AND BOTH ARE WRONG BY ONE TO TWO YEARS: the VRS reached Kopači only on 15 April 1994 (Volume II, PDF pp. 478-479) and entered the outskirts of Ustiprača only by 31 May 1993 (Volume II, PDF p. 409); neither was securely Serb-held in April 1992. (3) NAME-SEARCHING THE CANDIDATES GIVES A FALSE SIGNAL POINTING THE WRONG WAY: "glamoc" returns 65 hits, all the WESTERN Glamoč some 200 km away, and "kamen" 36 as a common placename root, while "sopotnica" and "podkozara" return zero — 101 hits steering toward two cells with no connection to this brigade, and silence on the one actually selected. FLAGGED, NOT ACTED ON — the corps field: this row carries "vrs_drina" at turn 0, but the Drina Corps formed 1 November 1992 and footnotes 117-121 place all five Podrinje brigades in Tactical Group "Višegrad" of the HERZEGOVINA Corps before that. Scenario-design question, affects the whole family. ALSO RECORDED, NOT ACTED ON: this leaves the 5th at Goražde and brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade at Višegrad, which is the correct APRIL 1992 pair. The post-1994 reality — both at Višegrad, merged under the 5th designator — is not represented and would need an event to model.
brigade:rs_5th_podrinje.notes: EVIDENCE SPLIT ACROSS TWO TIERS FOR TWO DIFFERENT FIELDS. Read them separately. (A) home_mun "gorazde" — SCHOLARLY, Balkan Battlegrounds, per the citation field above. (B) home_osid "op:gorazde:podkozara_donja_2" — SOURCE: NONE. This is an ENGINE PLACEMENT within the BB-attested municipality, and no part of the citation above supports it. The schema requires a home_osid (0 of 246 rows lack one) and history cannot supply one, so it is filled by a stated, reproducible rule rather than a preference: AMONG OSIDs IN THE BB-ATTESTED MUNICIPALITY, PREFER ONE OUTSIDE ANY GUARDED ENCLAVE KEY SPACE. That selects podkozara_donja_2 uniquely — verified against ENCLAVE_DEFINITIONS in src/sim/combat/enclave_resilience.ts, whose Goražde entry lists 18 OSIDs including glamoc, kamen and sopotnica, the other three RS-held candidates, and does NOT include podkozara_donja_2. It is the only real Goražde cell outside the guard. (C) home_settlement "" — LEFT EMPTY DELIBERATELY, because the settlement is not established. This is an existing encoding in the file, not a defect, and it is one of the two tells that exposed the Vlasenica error, so the signal is preserved rather than papered over. §6 REASONING FOR THE RULE, which is why it is a rule and not a tiebreak: this is a home assignment and not a collapse write, and the field guard is own-OSID, so no violation is in play. But homing a VRS brigade at turn 0 INSIDE the guarded key space would put an enemy formation in the guard's watched cells from turn zero, making "Goražde holds" partly contingent on combat resolved inside cells the guard monitors — an undesigned coupling in the one enclave the guard requires to hold. The unguarded cell means that coupling never exists. If anyone later proposes one of the three guarded cells, that is a §6 panel question and not a data decision. officer:hvo_siljeg.source: ICTY, Prosecutor v. Prlic et al., IT-04-74-T, Trial Judgement, 29 May 2013, Volume 2
officer:hvo_siljeg.citation: Trial Judgement Vol. 2, para. 13 - 'Zeljko Siljeg was Commander of the North-West OZ from October 1992 until 20 December 1993, whose headquarters were located at the Unis factory in Prozor'. Identity, command title, command dates and HQ all come from this one paragraph.
officer:hvo_siljeg.court_record_citation: NOT AN ACCUSED — findings only. ICTY, Prosecutor v. Prlic et al., IT-04-74-T, Trial Judgement, 29 May 2013, Vol. 2 (https://www.icty.org/x/cases/prlic/tjug/en/130529-2.pdf). Siljeg was not one of the six accused (Prlic, Stojic, Praljak, Petkovic, Coric, Pusic); the Chamber makes findings about him as a non-party. Command: Vol. 2 para. 13 — 'Zeljko Siljeg was Commander of the North-West OZ from October 1992 until 20 December 1993', HQ at the Unis factory in Prozor. Prozor arrests: para. 125 — 'By an order dated 6 July 1993, Zeljko Siljeg, Commander of the North-West OZ, instructed the Military Police and the SIS of the Rama Brigade to arrest and detain all Muslim men between the ages of 16 and 60 from Prozor Municipality'; para. 135 — 'The Chamber therefore finds that, at the order of Zeljko Siljeg, the Military Police [...] arrested Muslim men, including minors, elderly and sick people, in June, July and August 1993 in Prozor Municipality'; see also para. 1813. SCOPE SEPARATION — do NOT merge these three into one sentence: para. 125 is the ORDER AS ISSUED, scoped to Prozor Municipality via the Rama Brigade Military Police and SIS; para. 135 is the ARRESTS AS FOUND; para. 1813 is the DETENTION CONSEQUENCES and states the order's reach more broadly as 'the territory of the North-West OZ' (237 detainees from Prozor to Ljubuski Prison, relocated to Dretelj the next day for lack of space; a further ~155 from the Prozor secondary school to Ljubuski on 16 July 1993). The Prozor-Municipality and North-West-OZ scopes are not a contradiction but are not interchangeable — the player-facing summary deliberately uses the narrower para. 125 scope. Gornji Vakuf: para. 389 — 'On 21 January 1993, Colonel Zeljko Siljeg dispatched a report to the Chief of the HVO Main Staff, telling of the "cleansing" of the four villages attacked as described above.' Para. 367 — Dusa was 'one of the Muslim villages most devastated as a result of the HVO attack', and the Chamber refers to 'the report by Colonel Zeljko Siljeg, commander of the HVO's North-West OZ, dated 29 January 1993, that 18 houses were destroyed in Dusa, including two which had been shelled.' AUTHORITY, NOT CONDUCT — para. 320: 'On 24 October 1992, further to an order from Zeljko Siljeg, all the armed forces of the HVO in Gornji Vakuf Municipality, were subordinated to the command of the Ante Starcevic Brigade.' This is a COMMAND-SUBORDINATION finding and alleges nothing by itself. It establishes his authority and must NEVER be listed under a heading implying it is an attacks-on-civilians finding. Command knowledge, Prozor Oct 1992: para. 44 — he 'received a report from the Rama Brigade saying that the HVO was in control of Prozor town and the Lake Rama Sector and that each territory was "ethnically pure as the Muslim population has been detained or has fled"'.
officer:hvo_siljeg.verification_note: THIS CITATION IS CHECKABLE FROM INSIDE THE REPO — no external fetch required. The paragraphs above were read from the official ICTY PDF (icty.org/x/cases/prlic/tjug/en/130529-2.pdf), which the repo does not hold, so the numbering was validated against a citation the repo already had and which was produced independently of this work: brigade:hvo_rama_brigade cites 'Trial Judgment, Volume 2, paras. 13-15 - identifies the HVO Rama Brigade, its Prozor base, command succession, and North-West Operational Zone.' Paras 13-15 as read contain exactly those four things - the North-West OZ (13), the Unis-factory Prozor base (13 and 15), and the Rama Brigade command succession Franjic -> Beljo -> Zelenika -> Pavlovic (15). Two independently produced readings agreeing field for field establishes that the paragraph numbering used here is the judgement's own. Anyone re-checking this should compare those two records rather than re-fetch. THIS IS THE PATTERN TO COPY: when a tribunal citation cannot be verified in-repo, anchor it to an existing in-repo citation of the same document and record the agreement. Three independent extractions now agree on this numbering — the repo's original author, a pdftotext pass, and a PyMuPDF pass. METHOD WARNING, and it nearly produced a confidently wrong verbatim quote: a WHOLE-DOCUMENT paragraph splitter run over Vol. 2 returns FOOTNOTE TEXT for 'para 13' (footnotes 1045-1048, Uzricje/Gornji Vakuf), because footnote blocks also begin '13.'. Only a PAGE-SCOPED extraction, restricted to pages containing the officer's name, returns the true para. 13. Any future paragraph pull from an ICTY PDF must be page-scoped to the name. The failure mode is the dangerous one: the lookup returns something plausible rather than nothing, so the error does not announce itself.
officer:hvo_siljeg.conflict_note: SUPERSEDES a false record. This row previously carried, and the officer record asserted, a BiH State Court CONVICTION with a 10-year sentence for Prozor 1993. No such conviction exists in any source located: no case number, no date, no judgement. The conviction and sentence were removed as unsourced content the game must not ship (SENSITIVE_HISTORY_DESIGN_GATE.md Sec. 4), and the record was converted to the ICTY Prlic findings above, which are exact and tribunal-tier. DO NOT RESTORE 'convicted'. BiH proceedings against Siljeg exist but are at the INVESTIGATION / CHARGE stage, awaiting Croatian assistance to question him - open, never concluded. Asserting a conviction that does not exist is the same error as deleting a finding that does, committed in the other direction. If the open proceeding is ever recorded here it must be flagged OPEN and must not be typed as a verdict.

officer:vrs_zivanovic.court_record_citation: NOT AN ICTY ACCUSED. The ICTY indicted 161 individuals; Zivanovic is not among them, and he is not among the Srebrenica accused (Krstic, Blagojevic, Jokic, Obrenovic, Momir Nikolic, Erdemovic, the seven in Popovic et al., Tolimir, Karadzic, Mladic, Trbic). He appeared at the ICTY only as a defence witness for Karadzic in October 2013. ICTY LOCATIONS NAMING HIM, all verified against the operative Second Consolidated Indictment, Prosecutor v. Popovic et al., IT-05-88-PT, 14 June 2006: para. 34 (Count 2, Conspiracy to Commit Genocide) - '...entered an agreement with several others, including General Ratko Mladic, the Commander of the VRS; General Milenko Zivanovic, Commander of the Drina Corps through about 2000 hours on 13 July 1995; General Radislav Krstic...'; paras. 54 and 55 (the 2 July 1995 order; entering Srebrenica town with Mladic and Krstic after the fall); Attachment A, 'MEMBERS OF THE JOINT CRIMINAL ENTERPRISES', which lists him by name; background paras. 4-6 (appointed first Drina Corps commander on the corps' formation, 1 November 1992 - which independently matches BB2 p. 290 - serving 'until about 2000 hours on 13 July 1995'). In the earlier 26 March 2002 indictment the equivalents are paras. 20 and 23. HE IS NOT AN ACCUSED IN EITHER VERSION, and the check that shows it is typographic: the ICTY typesets accused in CAPITALS, and Mladic, Zivanovic, Krstic and Karadzic appear in normal case throughout. Being named in a pleading against other men is not being charged - this is the origin of the false 'ICTY / indicted' record corrected here. TRIAL JUDGEMENT FINDING on the orders: Popovic et al., IT-05-88-T, Trial Judgement, 10 June 2010 (https://www.icty.org/x/cases/popovic/tjug/en/100610judgement.pdf), para. 244 - 'On 2 July 1995, two orders, "Krivaja-95", were issued in the name of Zivanovic, the Drina Corps Commander.' Note the Chamber's wording: para. 243 attributes the drafting of the plan to Krstic, and the exhibits are type-signed rather than signed (Ex. 5DP00106, 'type-signed Milenko Zivanovic') - hence 'issued in his name' rather than 'signed by him' in the summary. HANDOVER: cite the indictment's 'about 2000 hours on 13 July 1995' (para. 34 and background paras. 4-6), which is primary and more precise than Popovic TJ para. 1104 (Mladic announcing his retirement and Krstic's appointment at Vlasenica on the afternoon of 13 July) or the in-repo docs/research/icty_rs_strategic_goals.md:148. BB2 p. 290's 'late July 1995' is the looser figure, not a contradiction. THE LIVE CHARGE IS BiH, NOT ICTY: the Prosecutor's Office of BiH Special Department for War Crimes filed an indictment in December 2021 for crimes against humanity in Srebrenica and Zepa, July 1995, as a JCE participant; the indictment was confirmed by the Court of BiH (confirmation DATE not established - first English report of the filing is 4 January 2022, so confirmation falls somewhere between December 2021 and early 2022; do not state a confirmation date). Case number NOT LOCATED - sudbih.gov.ba did not surface his case page; do not guess an S1-1-K number. After he failed to appear at three plea hearings the Court requested an international arrest warrant in 2023. He resides in Serbia. SEPARATE SERBIAN PROCEEDING, A DIFFERENT OFFENCE: Serbia charged war crimes against civilians covering 1992 AND 1995 conduct - not the BiH crimes-against-humanity charge for Srebrenica/Zepa 1995 - and the Higher Court in Belgrade acquitted him in July 2025 (secondary reporting is inconsistent between 1 and 2 July; state the month only). The acquittal does NOT dispose of the BiH indictment. The Belgrade Court of Appeals UPHELD the acquittal - it did not overturn it and did not order a retrial - so the acquittal is final and is the standing Serbian outcome. VERIFIED, but MEDIA-TIER and imprecisely dated: 17 June 2026 is the PUBLICATION date and could not be separated from the ruling date, and no Serbian court case number was obtainable. Do not state 17 June 2026 as the ruling date. Player-facing prose therefore says only 'upheld on appeal', with no date. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: this exculpatory finding is held to the same evidentiary standard as an inculpatory one, per the rule that an unsourced acquittal is the more dangerous kind because nobody instinctively challenges it. BiH and Serbian proceedings are media-tier, not tribunal-tier; flagged for /historian to upgrade with a Court of BiH case reference.
officer:vrs_zivanovic.conflict_note: SUPERSEDES a false record. The officer record previously asserted 'court: ICTY, verdict: indicted, charges: Genocide, crimes against humanity'. There is no ICTY indictment of Milenko Zivanovic and no genocide charge against him anywhere. The record also carried an unsourced clause, 'case referred to BiH State Court', which was a garbled gesture at a fact that is real and much stronger than the clause suggested: a confirmed Court of BiH indictment for crimes against humanity and an outstanding international arrest warrant. The correction therefore moves the court from ICTY to BiH State Court and the charges from genocide to crimes against humanity, and KEEPS verdict 'indicted'. It does NOT convert this record to 'named_in_findings' — doing so would tell the player that a man under a confirmed CAH indictment and an international warrant was never accused, which is a Sec. 4 minimisation and a worse error than the one being fixed.
officer:vrs_zivanovic.notes: Exact named identity and authored command context; gameplay ratings remain design-authored.
officer:vrs_zivanovic.verification_note: CITATION CORRECTION, recorded so the wrong number cannot be re-derived. An earlier draft of this row cited 'Popovic indictment paras. 96-97' for the JCE naming. That is WRONG and must not come back. The number was mis-read out of the Trial Judgement's own footnote apparatus: pdftotext merges footnote blocks onto single lines, and footnote 6440 ('Indictment, paras. 96-97') was attached to the JCE-membership passage when it belongs elsewhere - the adjacent footnote 6441 cites 'para. 98 (also alleging that the listed units, including the Scorpions Unit, participated in the JCE...)', which shows paras. 96-98 concern UNIT participation, not individually named members. That is exactly why a direct search of the operative indictment returns nothing about Zivanovic at 96-97. The correct individual-membership locations are para. 34 and Attachment A, read directly from the operative indictment. LESSON: a paragraph number lifted from a judgement's footnote is a citation of a citation; verify it against the cited document before it goes near a named person's criminal record. Popovic TJ footnote 3441 ('Ibid., para. 27') sits by the same membership passage and is UNVERIFIED against the operative indictment - it is left out of this row deliberately and is a cross-reference for /historian to check, not a claim.

brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade.source: Balkan Battlegrounds: A Military History of the Yugoslav Conflict, 1990-1995, Volume II
brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade.citation: Volume II, PDF p. 310 / printed 291, Drina Corps order-of-battle footnote 118: the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade was "Originally 1st Visegrad Light Infantry Brigade; merged with 5th Podrinje mid-late 1994." Footnote 121 gives the counterpart: the 5th Podrinje was "Originally 1st Gorazde Light Infantry Brigade; merged with 2nd Podrinje mid-late 1994, but retained 5th designator." Volume II, PDF p. 303 / printed 284 lists BOTH in the same order-of-battle block, the 2nd Podrinje flagged "(to mid-late 1994)". Volume II, PDF p. 416 / printed 397 footnote 42 glosses the trio as "1st Podrinje (Rogatica), 2nd Podrinje (Visegrad), and 5th Podrinje (Gorazde)".
brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade.conflict_note: PREVIOUSLY DELETED AS AN "EXACT ALIAS" OF rs_5th_podrinje. IT IS NOT AN ALIAS — IT IS A SEPARATE BRIGADE THAT WAS LATER MERGED INTO THAT ONE. The two units existed side by side from 1992 until the mid/late-1994 consolidation; AWWV starts in April 1992, so deleting this row asserted that consolidation roughly two and a half years early and left the Višegrad seizure without its anchor brigade. ARITHMETIC CORRECTION FOLLOWS FROM THIS: the alias de-duplication pass removed 2,700 phantom soldiers, not 3,500 — the three genuine HRHB duplicates only (Široki Brijeg 900, Grude 900, Čapljina 900). These 800 were never phantom, and any summary quoting 3,500 is wrong. NAMING CAVEAT, FLAGGED NOT CHANGED: at April 1992 the historically correct designation is "1st Višegrad Light Infantry Brigade"; the playable name "Višegrad Brigade" is acceptable as a generic, but "2nd Podrinje" would be anachronistic here because it postdates the Drina Corps. FLAGGED, NOT ACTED ON — SCENARIO-DESIGN QUESTION, NOT A DATA DEFECT: this row carries corps "vrs_drina" at turn 0, but the Drina Corps formed on 1 November 1992. Volume II footnotes 117-121 (PDF p. 310 / printed 291) place all five Podrinje brigades in Tactical Group "Višegrad" of the HERZEGOVINA Corps before that date. How AWWV should represent pre-Drina-Corps structure at an April 1992 start is a scenario-design decision and was explicitly not ruled on by the historian. Do not "fix" this row in isolation — it affects the whole Podrinje family.
brigade:rs_visegrad_brigade.notes: Exact formation identity and home region; the April 1992 existence of this brigade as a distinct unit is the sourced fact. Gameplay personnel, timing, and combat statistics are separately authored. Restored verbatim to its pre-deletion values.

brigade:hvo_hrvoje_vukcic_brigade.source: Balkan Battlegrounds: A Military History of the Yugoslav Conflict, 1990-1995, Volume II
brigade:hvo_hrvoje_vukcic_brigade.citation: FORMATION AND PARENT COMMAND (scholarly tier): Volume II, Annex 29, "Operation 'Vrbas 92': The VRS Assault on Jajce", PDF p. 349 / printed 330 — the HVO drew reinforcements "from the Central Bosnia Regional headquarters -- which had overall responsibility for Jajce - and the Northwestern Herzegovina Regional [headquarters]", and the defenders "were organized under the Jajce Municipal Headquarters, and probably consisted of about two battalions of local troops -- about 1,000 men". Volume II, PDF p. 352 / printed 333 tabulates it as "Jajce Municipal Headquarters (Brigade-equivalent) (+) / -2 local battalions: 1000 total personnel". NAME (project-KB tier): docs/knowledge/WIKIPEDIA_OOB_CROSS_REFERENCE.md:400 — "\"Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić\" Jajce | 97th | Jajce | Jajce | hr.wiki | NEW | 145 | Jajce fell Oct 1992. Remnants reconstituted in Prozor-Rama area." That row supplies the municipality (Jajce), the HQ (Jajce), the later 97th Home Guard designator and the casualty figure.
brigade:hvo_hrvoje_vukcic_brigade.conflict_note: PREVIOUSLY DELETED OUTRIGHT ON NAME GROUNDS. The deletion was right that the honorific does not belong to Odžak and wrong to conclude the formation should not exist: it belongs to JAJCE, and Jajce had zero brigades of any faction at turn 0 before this restore. TWO TIERS FOR TWO DIFFERENT FACTS, deliberately not merged: the FORMATION, its parent command and its strength are Balkan Battlegrounds-attested; the NAME "Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić" is project-KB tier via docs/knowledge/WIKIPEDIA_OOB_CROSS_REFERENCE.md:400 only. BB never uses the honorific — zero occurrences of "Hrvoje" in either volume, and the single "Hrvatini" hit is HRVATINI, an Adriatic border crossing in Slovenia (Volume I, PDF p. 100 / printed 63), not the person. Do not "confirm" the name off that hit. CORPS CORRECTED TO hvo_central_bosnia, AND THIS IS THE WRONG-YEAR TRAP AGAIN — THE FOURTH IN THIS CLUSTER. The obvious table, docs/knowledge/WIKIPEDIA_OOB_CROSS_REFERENCE.md:484, maps the 97th dom. puk. "(ex-Jajce)" to TOMISLAVGRAD. That is the POST-FALL reconstitution assignment: the remnants regrouped into the Prozor-Rama area, which sits in Tomislavgrad OZ. Implementing off that line would have reproduced the exact temporal-scope defect this whole pass exists to fix, inside its own fix. At April 1992 the parent is Central Bosnia, per BB2 p. 349/330 above. HOME OSID: op:jajce:jajce_3, the town, matching the sourced "HQ Jajce". The town is RBiH-controlled at turn 0 and that is deliberate and untouched — Jajce was defended jointly, BB2 p.352/333 also lists the ARBiH 705th Glorious Jajce Mountain Brigade there. A home_osid held by another faction at t0 is an established pattern in this file (six rows, including rs_visegrad_brigade and rs_1st_podrinje); no initial OSID control was overridden.
brigade:hvo_hrvoje_vukcic_brigade.notes: Exact formation identity, parent command, home region and approximate strength. Personnel 1,100 sits just above BB's "about 1,000 men" and is within authoring latitude; BB adds that only about two-thirds of the men were armed, which is an equipment/quality consideration for a later pass and NOT a reason to reduce personnel. FLAGGED, NOT ACTED ON — TWO CONSEQUENCES A LATER READER MUST NOT MISREAD. (1) THIS BRIGADE WAS DESTROYED, NOT MERELY DISPLACED. Jajce fell in October 1992 (the last stub at Karaula was, per Volume II PDF p. 351 / printed 332, "erased from the map 18 November"), and Volume I PDF p. 248 / printed 211 has the remnants "combined with two other destroyed shattered and exiled HVO units--the former 'Kupres' and 'Jajce' brigades--to form the 55th Home Defense Regiment". A Jajce brigade surviving intact to 1995 would be its own anachronism. Whether ordinary combat attrition handles that or it wants an explicit event is a scenario-design question for another seat — recorded so it is a conscious decision rather than a side effect. (2) THIS RESTORE WILL NOT BY ITSELF RECOVER THE JAJCE OSID CLUSTER, and a measurement that shows it has not is NOT the restore failing. Jajce was recovered by Croat forces on 13 September 1995 in Operation Maestral — Volume I, PDF p. 418 / printed 381: "Jajce -- the jewel of the operation--was restored to Croat hands, avenging its loss to the VRS in 1992." If the painted reference is the late-1995 line, Jajce is painted HRHB because of Maestral, not because of anything a turn-0 brigade does. The restore stands on its own merits: a municipality that historically held out for months against a VRS division should not open undefended.
